newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government suspends sale of Thomson.
newsitem.headline: French government suspends sale of Thomson.

text.p: The French Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it had suspended the sale of electronics and defence giant Thomson SA because an independent privatisation commission did not approve the sale of part of the group to Korea's Daewoo.
The government announced in October its preference for selling the state-owned group to Lagardere Groupe rather than rival bidder Alcatel Alsthom to create a competitive French defence giant.
Lagardere said it planned to sell consumer electronics division Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo, sparking an outcry from workers and the Socialist opposition.

The sell-off was conditional on approval by the European Commission, which has expressed reservations about government plans for an 11 billion franc ($2 billion) capital injection, and by France's privatisation commission.

That body "declared itself incapable of giving a favourable opinion to the Lagardere Groupe offer, because of the terms of Daewoo Electronics' purchase of Thomson Multimedia," the ministry said in a statement.

"Consequently, the government has decided to suspend the privatisation process under way," it said, adding that France remained committed to privatising Thomson, to ensure the company's own development and for the creation of a world-calibre French electronics sector.
